diagrams.title: From Unpaid Judgment to Monthly Payment Stream
diagrams.subtitle: Five intake and enforcement steps reported by judgment recovery operators
diagrams.caption: Operators screen out dead files first, confirm an attachable asset, rate collectibility, open contact by hard-copy letter, then garnish the bank and trade writ dismissal for a down payment plus monthly installments.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Step order combines the operator gates and pro-tips stated by each named practitioner; dollar figures are Rich Meyer's reported terms, not guaranteed outcomes.
diagrams.note: Sources - TheJRInstitute (3p5TZGrk1og), Default Investor Association with Rich Meyer (fjA8sRRh0ZI), Collect Back Rent Training Course with Cynthia Schmidt (5T2nU_IZTXs).

stages.label: Screen Bankruptcy and Death Records
stages.detail: TheJRInstitute checks bankruptcy filings and death records before preparing the assignment, so no work starts on a dead file.

stages.label: Confirm an Attachable Asset
stages.detail: Rich Meyer confirms an asset exists before signing the creditor, because exemptions such as head of household make wage and bank garnishment difficult.

stages.label: Rate and Refuse the Uncollectible 30 Percent
stages.detail: Cynthia Schmidt rates where the debtor moved, judgment size, and other judgments, and declines the roughly 30 percent she rates uncollectible.

stages.label: Mail a PIN Letter Before Any Email
stages.detail: TheJRInstitute mails a hard-copy letter with a PIN first, then uses that PIN to encrypt every later email to the debtor.

stages.label: Garnish the Bank, Then Trade Dismissal for Payments
stages.detail: Meyer garnishes for $188 and trades writ dismissal for $500 down plus $100 to $200 a month, reaching about $3,000 per month by the third month at ten files a month.

diagrams.title: Judgment Lien Survival Path on Real Property
diagrams.subtitle: Abstract, recording, interest, revival, and bankruptcy checkpoints
diagrams.caption: A money judgment becomes a lien on land only once abstracts are issued and recorded, then must accrue, be revived on time, and clear the bankruptcy lookback to keep its place in line.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Each stage value is the figure the cited practitioner stated for that step, in its own unit (originals, counties, percent, years, days); widths are not conversion counts.
diagrams.note: Sources - Bobby Benjy (hJmfkC9gu4c), David Babel (q6PjSqG-sF4), Five Minute Legal Master Series (V5NrY_biljg).

stages.label: Abstract Issued by the Clerk
stages.detail: In Bobby Benjy's worked example the LA County Superior Court clerk issued 3 sealed abstracts from the one-page California form.

stages.label: Recorded in Each Target County
stages.conversion: Orange, San Francisco, and Contra Costa through an attorney service
stages.detail: Benjy records in major counties plus every county where research shows the debtor owns land; a recorded abstract attaches when the debtor buys later.

stages.label: Lien Accrues Interest Until Payoff
stages.conversion: Payoff required before sale or refinance
stages.detail: David Babel describes a Bronx Supreme Court judgment lien accruing 9 percent a year that must be paid off even after a Chapter 7 discharge.

stages.label: Revival Filed Inside the Window
stages.conversion: Late revival survives but goes to the end of the line
stages.detail: Five Minute Legal Master Series sets the Pennsylvania revival deadline that keeps lien priority against intervening liens.

stages.label: Bankruptcy Lookback Cleared
stages.conversion: Liens filed inside the window can be avoided
stages.detail: Babel says a judgment lien filed within 90 days of filing can be avoided on a primary residence and on investment properties.

diagrams.title: Where a $10,000 Recovery Goes Under Contingency
diagrams.subtitle: Fee, expense, and lien deductions before the client is paid
diagrams.caption: A $10,000 settlement at a 33.33 percent contingency, a $250 expense reimbursement, and a medical lien negotiated from $500 to $350 leave a $6,066.67 client disbursement.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Figures come from the LeanLaw SettleFlow demo; the $6,416.67 subtotal is arithmetic on those figures. Delegation cost varies, with receivers typically taking 25 percent per Hendershot Cowart and collection agencies taking a third per Private Investigator Videos.
diagrams.note: Sources - LeanLaw (pmUaXhIL3eA), Hendershot Cowart P.C. (-kyDpaMUqFY), Private Investigator Videos (q-khGCaOPck).

diagrams.title: Deal Percentages on Assigned and Purchased Judgments
diagrams.subtitle: Splits, payback shares, fees, and garnishment ceilings quoted by practitioners
diagrams.caption: Operators keep one-third to one-half of collections, Lance runs a straight 50/50 split, Schmidt pays original creditors 15 to 20 percent on future-pay buys, and wage garnishment tops out at 25 percent of gross pay per Greg.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Where a practitioner gave a range, typical is either the figure they called standard or the arithmetic midpoint (17.5 for Schmidt's 15 to 20 percent). Single-figure claims show the same min, max, and typical.
diagrams.note: Sources - Cross the River, Find the Treasure (TiGcICs90xE), Judgment Recovery Training Online with Lance (L2dopNFjS6s), cynthia schmidt (t_Wf5tSZn4s), InfoUSA1 with Greg of Ford Judgment Recovery (OjrZdehs8Xk), LeanLaw (pmUaXhIL3eA).

bars.label: Operator Share of Collections
bars.display: One-third to one-half, 50 percent standard on small claims

bars.label: Lance Contingency Split
bars.display: 50/50 with no fees to the creditor

bars.label: Wage Garnishment Ceiling
bars.display: Up to 25 percent of gross pay per paycheck

diagrams.title: Wage Garnishment and Bank Levy Go/No-Go Gates
diagrams.subtitle: Four checks before relying on the state's collection machinery
diagrams.caption: The creditor must locate a job or bank, run the interest math, anticipate exemption fights, and stop cold on a bankruptcy notice; Mr. Grey's answer to thin accounts is a four-bank levy.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Gate order is an organizing sequence built from the cited operator gates; exemption amounts and caps are state-specific as reported for Arizona and Georgia.
diagrams.note: Sources - Consumer Warrior with John Skiba (YmCEqLCbD3s), Law Office of Jeffrey B. Kelly (cHsptp1ujiI), Westgate Law (Nb1quOaLNWk), Mr. Grey Judgment Enforcement (CLxNTh8V1qQ), Bobby Benjy (a13Ojjc6ruw).

nodes.question: Has a job or bank account been located for the debtor?
nodes.fail_action: Mine the credit report for employment and the old check or auto-debit trail for the bank, including spouse-name and joint accounts.

nodes.question: Does the garnishment outpace 28 to 30 percent contract interest?
nodes.fail_action: Do not rely on a 10 percent Arizona wage garnishment alone; add bank levies, and confirm a Georgia employer computes withholding correctly.

nodes.question: Is the frozen money free of exemptions?
nodes.fail_action: Expect fights over all-Social Security accounts, the roughly $5,600 Arizona account exemption that doubles for married couples, and adult-child money in joint accounts.

nodes.question: Is the file clear of any bankruptcy notice?
nodes.pass_next: Fire a four-bank levy at once and let any overage flow back to the debtor.
nodes.fail_action: Stop enforcement, return money taken after the filing, and track the sheriff and the bank.

diagrams.title: Collection Compliance Desk Under Regulation F
diagrams.subtitle: One accountable lead, four contact and evidence spokes
diagrams.caption: Regulation F turned contact limits into countable violations, so each channel gets a hard metric and the evidence file is built before any dispute reaches court.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Role names are an organizing frame; every KPI is a limit or practice stated by the cited attorneys and practitioners. Practitioners split on whether seven-in-seven is a hard cap or a presumption.
diagrams.note: Sources - SeniorLiving.Org with Kaiser Jansen (9RtU4rpS3pw), Night Ferry (7HVra7o-cZg), Saul Ewing LLP (MM_dCPRf9LE), Meet Jermaine (XSfDS_s1URg), LawShelf (i6PAssklgJg), Hard Hat Economics (-FdK6kbQiio).

center.headcount: The operator plus any staff, trained before the first call
center.focus: No abusive, unfair, or deceptive practices across every contact channel

spokes.kpi: No more than 7 call attempts per 7 days per account, none outside 8 a.m. to 9 p.m.
Simple opt-out on every text and zero contact after a stop reply
Validation notice within five days and representation letters processed the day they arrive
Every letter copied with its 16-digit certified tracking number against up to $1,000 statutory damages plus fees

diagrams.title: Debtor Examination and Follow-Up Levy Cost Stack
diagrams.subtitle: California filing and levy costs reported by practitioners
diagrams.total_range: $60 exam order with a free writ, then $30 to $1,500 or more in levy deposits, plus $300 per 8 hours if a keeper is used
diagrams.caption: The examination itself is cheap; the spend lands on the levies that must be ready to fire right after the exam, before the debtor moves money to a different bank.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Exam order and writ costs are Sacramento figures; levy deposit and keeper figures are California writ-of-execution costs from a separate source. The levy deposit high end is stated as $1,500 or more.
diagrams.note: Sources - Sacramento County Public Law Library (HrhPbWDRBVU), Lawyer Tips by The Sterling Firm (UV-WyQ1-NC4).

buckets.label: Examination Order Filing
buckets.notes: Sacramento fee, with a court backlog of up to a month or more and a 150-mile reach

buckets.label: Writ of Execution Issued With the Order
buckets.notes: Issued at the same time for free in Sacramento

buckets.label: Levy Deposits
buckets.notes: From bank and wage levies up to business and sale notices, $1,500 or more at the top

diagrams.title: Four-Week Judgment Lifespan Audit
diagrams.subtitle: Logging expiry, renewing, checking revival windows, and sizing defense risk
diagrams.caption: Judgments outlive the debts behind them only when renewal and revival deadlines are tracked; collectors who miss the window face debtors who check it.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The four-week sequence is an organizing frame, not a practitioner-reported timeline; lifespans, windows, and fees are as stated by the cited speakers and vary by state.
diagrams.note: Sources - The Business Guy (nbtlIEi4we0), Law Office of Richard Kistnen (bkM9l8fajkc), The Credit Repair Shop (--FOsBTlu2E, 4Mctc4AuqWA), Consumer Warrior with John Skiba (fWHpyqQu_5M).

weeks.title: Lifespan Audit
weeks.deliverable: Judgment date and state lifespan logged for every file, such as California 10 plus 10 and Oklahoma 5-year renewals indefinitely
weeks.gate: No file is worked until its expiry and renewal dates are calendared

weeks.title: Renewal Filing
weeks.deliverable: Renewals filed where due, a simple filing for another 10 years per Kistnen
weeks.gate: Renewal goes through when the debtor does not appear to challenge it

weeks.title: Revival Window Check
weeks.deliverable: State revival window checked against the original judgment date on every dormant purchased judgment
weeks.gate: Drop any revival past the window; one Ohio collector filed two years past a 10-year window

weeks.title: Lawsuit and Arbitration Posture
weeks.deliverable: New suits sized against AAA fees of about $200 for the consumer versus $2,500 to $5,000 upfront for the creditor
weeks.gate: About 95 percent of sued consumers default, but a $3,500 claim compelled into AAA arbitration usually ends in dismissal or a mutual walk-away
